title: Localize remaining modules (per-language domain reviewer)
context: After i18n-021 proves the localization process for one module and one target language, the remaining core modules can be localized per language. Each language requires a distinct domain-qualified reviewer (fluent in the target language and with cancer bioinformatics expertise). Risk is medium because any localized module containing a worked example retains the data gate requirement. This is a backlog item: it should only proceed after i18n-021 is complete and has validated the process for at least one language.
objective: Localize remaining core modules into additional target languages following the process established in i18n-021, with a domain-qualified reviewer for each language, CC-BY-4.0 attribution preserved, and no accessibility regressions introduced.
acceptanceCriteria: Remaining core modules localized into >= 1 additional target language(s), following the directory structure and process established in i18n-021.
Each language has a named domain-qualified reviewer (fluent in target language + cancer bioinformatics expertise) who signs off on technical accuracy and terminology appropriateness.
Educator reviewer confirms cognitive load, accessibility, and pedagogical structure are maintained for each localized module.
If any localized module contains a worked example with a cancer dataset, the data gate (datagate-002) applies: PASS gate artifact must be committed or confirmed valid for the localized version.
CC-BY-4.0 attribution preserved and correct in all localized versions; original authorship credited.
No accessibility regressions: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance maintained; i18n-readiness of source modules confirmed.
Localized modules committed to the repo in language-scoped directories; DCO signed off.
resources: PLAN.md (Sustainability — adoption beyond the authors; M3 — localization)
datagate-002 (applies to any localized worked example)
WCAG 2.2 AA; Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0 attribution requirements
output: Remaining core modules localized into >= 1 additional target language(s), committed in language-scoped directories; domain-qualified and educator reviewer sign-offs per language; no accessibility regressions.
